docs(roadmap): F9 measured - 1.26x decode, 1.14-1.17x prefill
  node                        F8          F9    F9/F8   vs pristine
  K=51 decode  nrows=2    457,092     362,799    1.26x    12.34x

  K=56 prefill nrows=4  6,636,852   5,683,029    1.17x        -

The finding worth keeping is that decode and prefill are now bound by
different things. Cycles per issued instruction: the gemv is unchanged at
2.23 -> 2.24, so it is purely issue bound and F9 converted the instruction
saving 1:1 into cycles. The gemm's went 2.53 -> 4.84, so it is not issue
bound any more and cutting instructions further will not help prefill.
Corollary: F8's "instruction-issue floor" of 328,865 was never a floor, it
was an instruction count - F9 beat it at 362,799 with no HVM.

Also records the two things that did NOT work, so nobody repeats them:
grouping the widths in source (the scheduler undoes it, 4.00 -> only 2.00),
and 4 scratch registers instead of 2 (no spills, but 855,476 vs 818,314,
4.5% worse - so producer-consumer distance is not the gemm's limiter).
The experiment that would identify it, d4-nopf and d4-hvm on the prefill
node, is written down but not yet run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
perf(riscv): F9, one vsetvli per four dots instead of four per dot
The Q1_D4 kernels alternate between the byte view (mask load, sign expand)
and the 32-bit view (activation broadcast, the dot). Every alternation costs
a vsetvli that does no arithmetic: 4 per dot in the gemv, 40% of its inner
loop. GCC's share of that is that it cannot see inside an inline asm block,
so it assumes each one left vtype unknown and re-issues its own.

Grouping the two widths in the source is NOT enough - the scheduler
interleaves them again. Measured: source grouping alone only got the gemv
from 4.00 to 2.00 vsetvli per dot. So everything at e32 now lives inside one
asm block, the broadcasts included, leaving GCC only e8 work to schedule.

  vsetvli per dot (between first and last dot, O3): gemv 4.00 -> 0.94
                                                    gemm 2.00 -> 0.52
  instrs per dot:                                   gemv 10.00 -> 7.90
                                                    gemm  9.00 -> 4.13
The gemm gains more because the smaller body also let GCC unroll its column
loop 8x, which it would not do before. No vector spills.

Taking the activation quads as uint32 GPRs and spelling out vmv.v.x also
kills the vlse32 stride-0 trap by construction, so q1_bcast_act4 and its
barrier are gone.

Bit-identical, not just close: test-repack-q1_0 13/13 with every nmse
unchanged from the pre-F9 run (0.000e+00 on the gemv cases, 4.171e-15 /
1.282e-14 / 7.417e-15 on the gemm ones). Q1_D4=0 control also 13/13.
check-vd4dots.sh gains a VTYPE-CHURN budget of 1 vsetvli per dot, which
fails on the old code at O3 and passes now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
docs(roadmap): correct the F9 cause - e8/e32 ping-pong, not the asm
The entry blamed GCC re-emitting vsetvli after the inline asm. That is real
but it is only 1 of the 4 vsetvli per dot. The dominant cause is that the
work alternates between the byte view (vlm, vmerge) and the 32-bit view
(vmv.v.x, dot), and every alternation costs one - it would happen with no
inline asm at all. Widening the asm block therefore recovers 1 of 4, not
4 of 4; the fix is to batch by element width. Includes the real O3 listing
and marks the 1.5x as an instruction count, not measured cycles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
